newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt to issue decree on trucker hours.
newsitem.headline: French govt to issue decree on trucker hours.

text.p: French junior transport minister Anne-Marie Idrac said on Friday the government will sign a decree defining working hours for truckers in a bid to end blockades crippling the country's economy.

"The impact (of the 12-day-protest) on citizens and on the economy is becoming dramatic in certain areas," Idrac said. She urged truckers to lift their blockades before the decree is issued, in two weeks time at the most.

Haulage bosses and employers are due to meet at 9.30 a.m. (0830 GMT) to sign six deals settling most of the truckers' demands, including a pledge on payment for all working hours including time spent loading.

"But people have said for years that the issue (of working hours) must be settled and we need to go further. We must clarify in an irrefutable manner what working hours should involve, what should be paid for. We need a decree," Idrac said.

She said the government would need up to 15 days to draw up a decree because the issues were complex and it had to consult the parties involved in the dispute that has seen a blockade of roads, freight depots and refineries enter its twelfth day.
"During those 15 days the blockades must be lifted. The decision to sign this decree has been taken," she said.
